messages:
Kevin: Quick perf note — saw a regression on sm95 for quantized paths after the autotune change. p50 up ~22% for seq > 2048. Posting raw profile and logs below, any immediate thoughts?

Sasha: Saw this in nightly too. Looks like runtime is falling back unexpectedly at dispatch time. Could be workspace calc or a kernel mismatch.

Priya: Can you paste the decision logs? curious whether autotuner selected an int4 kernel or if the runtime forced fp8.

Kevin: Here's the relevant extract from the agent log around dispatch (redacted):
```
[2026-03-16 03:12:42] choose_kernel: model=redwood-7b quant=INT4 arch=sm95 candidates=[int4_sm95_kv_opt, int8_sm95_default, fp8_sm95_fallback]
[2026-03-16 03:12:42] autotuner: preferred=int4_sm95_kv_opt score=0.82 workspace_needed_bytes=2899104000
[2026-03-16 03:12:42] runtime: free_workspace_bytes=2684354560 -> insufficient, falling back to fp8_sm95_fallback
[2026-03-16 03:12:42] dispatch: picked=fp8_sm95_fallback
```
Simple summary: autotuner chose int4 (based on perf model) but runtime dropped to fp8 due to workspace shortfall. The switch costs a lot of KV cache churn and increases latency for long seqs.

Lee: That pattern explains the regression. Two levers we should consider: (1) increase workspace safety margin for sm95 autotuner so it prefers kernels that fit the common available workspace, (2) add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping on per-request basis.

Lee: Proposal (quick config):
```
quant_autotune:
  arch_overrides:
    sm95:
      workspace_margin_pct: 15  # was 8
      min_stable_requests: 40   # was 10
      seq_thresholds:
        prefer_int8_above: 1024
```
This bumps margin and requires 40 stable successes before switching. Adds an explicit sequence-length rule to bias towards int8 for long sequences which are cache-sensitive.

Priya: I also think we should update the per-arch quant profile to reflect memory access patterns — on sm95 int4 kernels show worse streaming memory locality at long sequences. I'll run a micro-benchmark sweep: int4 vs int8 vs fp8 for seq=256/1024/4096. @perf-bot can you schedule? :thumbsup:

Kevin: Plan sounds good. If sweep confirms, we should revert the 'prefer_aggressive_int4' flag for sm95 and push the overrides. Will hold rollback 9f3a1c3 if needed.

perf-bot: perf-sweep finished for sm95 (commit=9f3a1c3):
- seq=256: int4 p50=42ms, int8 p50=48ms, fp8 p50=50ms
- seq=1024: int4 p50=120ms, int8 p50=115ms, fp8 p50=125ms
- seq=4096: int4->fp8 path p50=230ms (+24% vs baseline fp8), int8 p50=180ms (+4% vs baseline), baseline fp8 p50=210ms (+10%)
Links: https://perf.internal/sweeps/183600 || artifacts attached

Sasha: Those numbers line up with what we feared. For long seqs int8 is actually the best stable choice on sm95. Suggested action:
- revert prefer_aggressive_int4 on sm95 (short-term rollback)
- apply config overrides from Lee (workspace_margin_pct=15, min_stable_requests=40)
- add seq_threshold prefer_int8_above=1024
- run canary on dedicated pool for 24h
I'll open a PR for the config changes and the rollback. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/742

Priya: I'll add a unit test to the autotuner harness that simulates low-workspace scenarios and ensures the runtime-stable pick is used (no flip to fallback during the same request). Also adding evals to catch latency regressions for seq >= 1024.

Kevin: Thanks team. Action items: Sasha PR + canary, Priya tests/evals, Lee update tuning docs. If canary looks good we can re-enable a more aggressive int4 policy with stricter workspace checks later.

Lee: One more note — track KV cache warmup metric in the rollout dashboard. The early warmup slope diverges when we flip kernels; that will be our early warning.

Perf-bot: Canary scheduled on dedicated/cpu-gpools-12 for 24h starting 2026-03-16T09:00Z. Will report. :robot_face:
